content.text:
Verdict: the root cause and primary fix direction are sound, but this is not ready for PR. There are three implementation blockers plus a separate package-release gap.

## Review findings

1. High: documented relative data paths remain broken.

`file://.` is the recommended scaffold value in [init.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/embedded-pg-root-fix/packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts:382), but [ensureEmbeddedPgTraversal](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/embedded-pg-root-fix/packages/server/src/embedded-runtime.ts:197) walks lexical paths. For `.lobu`, it reaches `.` and stops without traversing the absolute parents of the current directory.

I reproduced this: the helper changed the project directory from `0700` to `0701`, but its parent remained `0700`, so the postgres user would still receive `EACCES`. Normalize targets to absolute paths and add a relative-path regression test.

2. High: the fix weakens `/root` and arbitrary ancestors for every local user.

The implementation applies `o+x` and asserts that root-mode containers, pods, and VPSes are single-tenant and that traversal “exposes no file contents” in [embedded-runtime.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/embedded-pg-root-fix/packages/server/src/embedded-runtime.ts:187). Neither assumption is generally true:

- VPSes and WSL hosts can be multi-user.
- Execute-only directories prevent listing, but files with known paths remain accessible according to their file modes.
- The permission change is durable after Lobu exits.
- A user-supplied embedded path can cause this behavior on directories beyond `/root`.

The access strategy needs an explicit security decision before shipping. Recommended direction: narrowly grant the postgres identity access using an ACL or equivalent. If broad `o+x` remains as a fallback, restrict it to confidently detected single-tenant containers or an explicit opt-in; host root mode should fail with actionable instructions rather than silently weakening `/root`.

3. Medium: chmod failures are swallowed, so the original unhandled crash still survives.

At [embedded-runtime.ts:212](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/embedded-pg-root-fix/packages/server/src/embedded-runtime.ts:212), a read-only mount or failed chmod is ignored. The subsequent `initdb` spawn then still dies with the dependency’s unhandled `EACCES`.

The helper should verify the postcondition and throw a clear Lobu-owned error listing inaccessible components. Add a regression test with `chmod` failure or an injected filesystem operation.

## What is verified

- Focused suite: 3 files, 13 tests passed together.
- `packages/server` typecheck: green.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- Retained pod `lobu-e2e-pgfix` is running and `/tmp/green.log` proves:
  - Postgres initialized through `/root`
  - database accepted connections
  - migrations completed
  - runtime reached application bootstrap
- The final encryption-key exit is expected.
- The original red log is only preserved in the handover, not `/tmp/red.log`; recapturing it would strengthen the PR evidence.

Repository state has also drifted:

- Worktree HEAD: `ee182a6db`
- Current `origin/main`: `6194aabdf`
- Branch is behind by two commits.
- Changes remain uncommitted: one modified source file and one untracked test.
- No remote branch or PR exists.

## Remaining plan

1. Resolve the three findings above and add tests for:
   - relative `file://.` paths behind a restrictive parent;
   - chmod/access-grant failure;
   - the selected secure access policy.

2. Rerun the focused three-file suite, server typecheck, and root-pod red→green reproduction. Preserve exact modes and logs.

3. Explicitly stage the two intended files into a WIP commit, fetch, and rebase onto current `origin/main`. Never stash.

4. Run `make pre-pr`, then `make review-fix`; reread both files afterward. If the fixer changes anything, rerun the relevant tests and gate.

5. Produce a settled commit and verify:
   - clean `git status`;
   - `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` contains exactly the two task files;
   - diff stat contains no Owletto pointer or unrelated server files.

6. Push, open the PR with full red→green output and permission modes, then run `make review` once. Merge only after every required check reports green.

7. Deliver through npm, not merely GitHub:
   - GitHub is at `14.10.0`, but npm still serves `@lobu/cli@14.8.0`.
   - The 14.9 and 14.10 publish workflows failed because they raced still-running `build-images` jobs; those image jobs are green now.
   - Treat repairing that publish race as a separate concern. For this fix’s eventual release, ensure package publishing is rerun after images are green.
   - Verify the actual published version using a fresh `node:22-bookworm` container and `npx -y @lobu/cli@<version> run`.

8. Only after evidence is copied into the PR, remove both retained pods and local packing artifacts. File the dependency’s missing child-process error-handler issue separately.

content.text: I’m replacing the world-readable traversal workaround with a scoped permission lease: Lobu will resolve/create the postgres OS identity before spawning, grant only that group execute access on the required ancestors, normalize relative and symlinked paths, fail with an actionable error if any grant cannot be established, and restore original ownership/modes after PostgreSQL stops or boot fails. This keeps the root E2E working without leaving `/root` open to every local account.

content.text: The first focused run caught a real edge case before E2E: Unix permission selection uses the owner class before group/other, so an identity that already owns a directory needs `u+x`, not `g+x`. content.text: why do we need those tests if we're getting rid of watchers everywhere?

We are not removing `watchers` everywhere. Per the repo invariant, `watcher` remains the internal engine/database vocabulary; only public APIs, SDK discovery, and UI must say “Behavior.”

This test protects that exact boundary:

- Internal DB query: count rows from `watchers`
- Public API response: expose `behaviorCount`
- UI: consume `behaviorCount`

Without it, the server returned `watcherCount`, while Owletto expected `behaviorCount`, silently showing zero Behaviors. The red test reproduced that real contract failure. I’ll keep the internal SQL terminology and test only the public Behavior-facing wire contract.
do you think we can't change everything?

content.text: The fixer found and repaired a genuine release blocker: GitHub returns workflow paths as `build-images.yml@<ref>`, so the old exact-path guard would have rejected every package publish. Release 14.11.0 is live and healthy. One manual GitHub setting remains before Helm is publicly installable.

Completed:

- Merged all fixes and release PRs, including Helm fail-closed guard #2459.
- Published all eight npm packages at `14.11.0`.
- Production reports healthy at exact release SHA `9123dd141ea72dfcc89d5ec09afa440eb68ccffd`.
- Deployment has two available replicas running chart/app `14.11.0`.
- Published CLI root E2E passed:
  - Running: ancestors became `0710 root:postgres`.
  - Health: HTTP 200.
  - SIGTERM: embedded Postgres shut down and every ancestor restored to `0700 root:root`.
- Public naming gate passed across SDK, API/MCP schemas, ClientSDK, connector SDK and CLI output.
- Internal database/engine names and their tests may still use `watcher`; the unsafe wholesale internal rename PR #2452 remains closed.
- Session pod and worktrees were removed. Existing unrelated untracked files were preserved.

Remaining action: change [`charts/lobu` package visibility](https://github.com/orgs/lobu-ai/packages/container/package/charts%2Flobu/settings) from **Private** to **Public**. GitHub documents visibility as a package-settings operation and does not provide a REST visibility-update endpoint. [GitHub package visibility documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud%40latest/packages/learn-github-packages/configuring-a-packages-access-control-and-visibility?apiVersion=2022-11-28), [REST Packages API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/packages/packages?apiVersion=2022-11-28).

Right now an anonymous Helm pull correctly returns `401`. Once you change that setting, tell me and I’ll verify `helm show chart ... --version 14.11.0` anonymously.
